page_note: Page is overwhelmingly Manichaean ecclesial institution material — a sustained discourse on catechumens (those who 'do not come to a body'), their relation to the holy church, almsgivings, the pearl simile, repentance, the Treasure of Life citation, and the catechumen's ascent. Teaching purity 0.000. Several segments deploy correspondential imagery (pearl, ripe fruits on tree, icons, country of the beautiful ones) but always as SIMILE applied to catechumen practice — the imagery is in service of an institutional argument. Significant editorial fatigue with seam at i=27 ('For this reason indeed it is fitting for the catechumen that he pray...'). No extractable cosmological substrate on this page.

segments.temporal_note: 'gathered there into the holy church' — institutional category.
Coming inward to the church — ecclesial movement.
Wife/kinsman — catechumen's social relations (institutional context).
Rejoicing over those who come in — institutional warmth.
Continuation: places his entire face upon them — ecclesial.
'Behold, this is the sign and type of the catechumens' — explicit institutional pivot, didactic framing.
'Catechumens who do not come to a body' + pearl simile applied to them — pearl imagery is correspondential but here functions as ecclesial illustration.
Citation of Mani's own work 'Treasure of Life' — late authorial self-reference, classic editorial citation formula.
Pearl 'has no equal value' — simile applied to catechumen state.
Catechumens explicitly named.
'Catechumens who do not come to a body' — continuation.
Soul-leaving-body theme but framed as catechumen fate.
Continuation of catechumen post-mortem path.

Icon/image language but applied to mercy of catechumens.

Almsgivings of catechumens — institutional practice.
'A body' — completion of catechumen formula.
'Concerning the rest of the catechumens' — institutional taxonomy.
'I have written down in the Treasure of Life' — Mani's authorial self-citation.

'According to his works' inward to the church — explicit ecclesial destination.
Catechumen's going-up — ecclesial soteriology.
Ascension and purification of catechumen.

'Reckoned unto his honor' — institutional recompense.
